campaign: Integrated validation, phase 2: bounded capability gains and evidence-gated simplification
doctrine:
overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data, promote or revert), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The milestone is the loop itself (improvement-loop): from there, the scorecard's gaps generate the work. Progress is counted in promotions, not landings: a cycle that measured, trained or changed, judged on held-out data and moved main. While main trails the landings since its last promotion, rows that close the cycle rank above rows that only harden or slim it, and a cycle that cannot finish (killed, withheld) outranks every other row.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing owner and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing owner can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced, and a run leaves its evidence complete by its own contract (every protocol a suite's acceptance asks for), never half-written for a later landing to trip on.

The landing gate judges the commit; the improvement cycle judges the models. The gate's verdict depends only on the tree: unit, golden, hermetic-fixture and small-device checks. Suites that load real models, read the live store's evidence or sweep the device belong to the cycle, declared by build tag, and promotion of main requires them on the commit it promotes; a store write never changes a landing's verdict. A change's landing cost is read from its diff as three independent effects: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost, so false lane reach is cut. A surface move also expires every evaluation bound to the surface, so the re-evaluation it forces counts in its cost: surface changes are batched and land before an evaluation run, never between its runs, and the guards are re-acquired once after the last of them. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a user-facing result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract, whether it moves to the cycle or is deleted; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

A step's verify fails before the change and passes after; a verify that already passes proves nothing, so a boundary is proved by the table row that fails today. Before a landing, what the gate refuses cheaply is run locally first: the claims check after any hand edit, the invariant tables, the rules' budget and exports, and the step's verify. A refusal found after the lanes costs an hour, and a retried landing rebuilds an identical gate binary.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the owner reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

Landing speed is protected by observing it, not by a rule. Each structural boundary (a changed path's lanes, a package kept off the inference surface, a suite kept to the cycle) is pinned as an invariant row in one table per kind, never as a new test function or a snapshot of today's lists. At each periodic review the gate's measured lines in git log are read: the share of landings that reached no lane, lane minutes per landing, and executed versus cached package counts. A rise means a misplaced check or a new false reach, fixed by moving it and adding a table row. There are no time budgets or timeouts, no ratchet baselines, and no separate tracking subsystem.

Training research is measured at the lowest cost that answers the question, reusing what exists. Optimizer math stays on the device: host Muon on the tied embedding cost about 98 s a step, and moving it took a 540-step run from about 21 hours to 6 minutes. During training only scalars cross to the host (losses, norms, brake decisions), never weights or gradients per step. Reuse comes before acquiring: cached base losses keyed by the exact window plan, existing checkpoints, held-out sets and the verdict code, before any new dataset, pass or tool. An evaluation beats a training run, a norm beats a decomposition, and a one-time computation beats a per-step one. For a training rate question the order is: post-hoc tests on existing checkpoints, then the held-out brake from the training forward against cached base losses, then a per-layer relative step size, and per-direction spectral scaling last.

items.title: Fuse the small decode kernels around the matmuls: norm, residual, scale and activation

steps.title: Fuse the small decode kernels around the matmuls: norm, residual, scale and activation
steps.rationale: Serves: inference (throughput) for E4B and gemma-12B. Evidence (2026-10-04, Nsight Systems, a decode token): gemma-4-12B fp8-native 22.1 ms wall and 21.0 ms of GPU kernels, of which matmuls (mul_mat_fp8 10.4, mul_mat_bf16 5.2) and the lm-head (2.05) read weights at the device bandwidth, and 3.2 ms is everything else: weighted_rms_norm 1.4 ms (289 launches a token at about 5 us), attention_decode 1.3 ms (47 launches at 28 us, latency-bound at short context), add, rope, multiply, gelu, copy at about 0.5 ms; E4B has the same classes at 2.9 ms. Weight bytes cannot shrink without changing outputs, so this 3 ms (about 14 percent of the step) is the remaining kernel-side gap. Disappears: launches, not code, if the fused kernels replace the separate ones and their tests; fusing sums in the same order keeps outputs identical, which a golden capture over the unmodified kernels proves (the Bonsai row's pattern). Batch: kernels and internal/cuda are pinned media runtime paths (a reviewed delta with a device receipt) and move the inference surface; batch with e4b-decode-graph.

items.title: Replay E4B's decode as a CUDA graph, as gemma-12B's already is

steps.title: Replay E4B's decode as a CUDA graph, as gemma-12B's already is
steps.rationale: Serves: inference (throughput) for gemma-4-E4B-it. Evidence (2026-10-04, Nsight Systems 2025.1.3 on the RTX 4090 D, cmd/benchmark -tokens 64 at 72bc4248d, three decodes of 64 tokens): E4B-bf16 decodes at 57.9 tok/s, 17.3 ms a token, with 0 graph launches, about 1,040 kernels launched one by one a token, and GPU kernel time of 12.9 ms a token, so about 4.4 ms (a quarter of the step) is launch and host gaps. The matmul and lm-head kernels read about 9.3 GB of weights in 10 ms, which is the device's bandwidth (about 0.93 TB/s of 1.0), so they cannot be sped up; the rest of the gap to the weight-read bound (9.2 ms, 108 tok/s) is non-matmul kernels at 2.9 ms (weighted_rms_norm 1.1, attention_decode 0.9). gemma-4-12B fp8-native, which replays a graph (63 launches in 64 tokens), loses only 1.1 ms of 22.1 to gaps. Disappears: nothing; this adds E4B to the graph path 12B uses, through the same capture owner. Evidence for the verify: graph_launches in the benchmark's own record is 0 for E4B and nonzero after. Batch: internal/inference and the kernels path are on the inference surface, so land with the next surface move. First find why E4B decode is not captured (per-layer embedding or altup ops with host-visible state?) before adding any mechanism.

items.title: Measure whether a per-step relative Muon rate transfers across models

steps.title: Measure whether a per-step relative Muon rate transfers across models
steps.rationale:
Owner proposal 2026-10-02: derive Muon's rate per layer from the layer, a per-step relative size rho*||W||/||U||, with a held-out brake (paired against the base's per-window loss) and no first-step line search (the 200-window sweep showed the short horizon favours the rate that later drifted). Measured: relative movement over 540 steps scales linearly with the rate; the good run moved matrices 0.8-1.4% (about 2.4e-5 per step), the old rate 6-10%; equal total movement is not equal outcome; 1-D norms and biases move 50-100x less relatively (tmp/relative_movement.go). On Qwen2.5-0.5B matrix weight scales differ at most 1.5x, so the per-layer rule cannot be told from the exponent there. Step: calibrate rho on 0.5B in the scratch sweep harness, then measure a second model; add its measured band as a row of TestDerivedRateFineTunesMeasuredModels; adopt the per-layer rule only if it transfers where the exponent does not; measure the 1-D tensors separately. Serves: train.

Post-hoc evaluation 2026-10-02 (no training; the good run's change, held-out 56 records, host log loss; scratch train3-wt zz_projection_eval_test.go): base 2.5508 (accuracy 0.4936); full change 2.3038 (0.5143, 56/56 records improve); inside W's row and column spaces 2.3913 (65% of the gain); singular-value part 2.5496 (none); rotation part 2.3913; outside W's spaces only 2.2933 (0.5171, beats the full change); full change except q and o 2.2964; q and o only 2.4966. Paired, removing the q/o change: Hodges-Lehmann -0.0074 nats, block-bootstrap 95% [-0.0086, -0.0066], 55/56 records improve. Conclusions: the learning lives mostly in the rectangular layers and outside their current spaces, so the subspace-restricting spectral rules are dropped, and so is the singular-value-only rule; the square attention matrices' update, where weak directions moved 100-240x more than strong ones, slightly hurts in combination. Per layer kind the drifting run's excess was uniform (6.9-7.5x against a 7.35x rate), but within kinds q/k/v relative movement spreads up to 6x across layers. Next arms on the device, paired held-out log loss, replicated on a second model: plain Muon at parameters^-0.6; q and o at a damped relative step; spectral scaling on q and o only if damping helps. Arms 2026-10-03 (Qwen2.5-0.5B, 540 steps of 512 tokens, frozen lexical, the policy's rate 6.078e-06, scratch train5-wt TestZZQORateArms; a per-matrix rate scale on the device Muon step, not landed): plain held-out log loss 2.3042 (token accuracy 0.5144); q and o at a quarter of the rate 2.3004, paired against plain Hodges-Lehmann -0.0034 nats, block-bootstrap 95 percent [-0.0043, -0.0025], 47 of 56 records improve; q and o not trained (scale 1e-9) 2.2997, HL -0.0042 [-0.0054, -0.0034], 48 of 56. Token accuracy does not move (0.5143 to 0.5145). So the square attention matrices' update costs about 0.004 nats of the run's 0.25-nat gain, damping recovers most of it and not training them recovers all: there is nothing for a spectral rule on q and o to win here, and that arm is dropped. Remaining: replicate plain against untrained q and o on a second model (MiniCPM5-1B, a 1B Llama-shaped model with an untied head, ZZ_MODEL in the same harness) before any policy change; the candidate rule is the simplest one, leave q and o untrained when fine-tuning, which also shrinks the update.

Fold landed 2026-10-01 without re-pointing the 12 coverage-proof Verify strings that name ./cmd/compatibility (11 text-vision, 1 image-video). Each proof's stored gate step binds the sha256 of its exact Verify string (internal/runrecord/completion_evidence.go:38-41, checked via media_coverage.go:400-406). Re-pointing them fails six acceptance tests ('completion acceptance evidence does not match the plan authority'), and nothing in the tree produces these gate records: formatCompletionAcceptanceEvidence has no non-test caller. The re-pointing is built in the scratchpad's compatfold-repoint.patch (new digests: text-vision 62ebc6e5..., image-video 6bf91882...). It applies together with re-acquired records once a producer exists, or the proofs retire against a replacement that covers their contract. Until then the strings name a command that no longer exists, as recorded history.

Deferred 2026-10-02 below the rows that can progress: the census needs the owner's review of the 11 identities the live catalog adds (snapshot 209, live 220), and re-acquiring the accepted baselines with realized residency needs the GPU. decisions.question: The scorecard's serving cells (first-output, throughput, load-time, peak-device-memory) aggregate every attempt a recipe ever made: medians over all time, total tokens over total decode time, the highest peak ever. A landed improvement shows only as old samples are outnumbered and a peak never falls. Since delete-selection each cycle measures every serving cell once at the measured commit. Should those cells read the newest successful measured attempt instead, accepting one sample's timing noise in each cycle's moved list?
options: newest measured attempt
all-time aggregates
median of the newest few attempts

decisions.question: Held-out quality is unscored for forecast, image-embedding, image-gen, seq2seq, tabular and vqa because each needs a held-out set the store lacks. Answering authorizes exactly these downloads into the datasets root, each to be verified by hash once fetched: ETTh1 (github.com/zhouhaoyi/ETDataset, 2.6 MB, forecast); BFCL v3 simple (gorilla-llm/Berkeley-Function-Calling-Leaderboard, 0.3 MB, seq2seq); BeyondArena credit-g (TabArena/BeyondArena, 0.2 MB, tabular); TIFA v1.0 (github.com/Yushi-Hu/tifa, 10 MB, image-gen); A-OKVQA validation (HuggingFaceM4/A-OKVQA, 60 MB, vqa); Imagenette 160 px (fast.ai imagenette2-160, 100 MB, image-embedding). About 173 MB in all. The other five unscored rows (generation, projection, speech, training, video-gen) use sets already on disk and are not blocked.
options: Download all six (about 173 MB)
Download only the four under 11 MB (ETTh1, BFCL, credit-g, TIFA)
Download none and score only what is on disk

decisions.question: The newest promoted scorecard (main = 5455dc909) predates comparison authority, so every evaluation cell in it reads Unknown to the code that now judges promotion and no candidate can promote against it. Cycle 10 (48d44c5b4) measured every blocking cell, passed every lane and published a record whose evaluation cells carry comparison authority, and was withheld only for that reason. Every baseline held-out quality holds by value against that record (83 hold, none regressed; the 3 cells a loose match flags are other contracts of the same suites, and the baseline's own cell is carried there by the same source evaluation with the same value). May the promoted branch move once, outside the cycle, to that commit?
options: Yes, move main once to 48d44c5b4 and promote normally after
No, relax the Unknown rule for baselines that carry no comparison authority
No, keep main and wait for an owner move
decisions.recommendation: Yes, move main once to 48d44c5b4 and promote normally after
